_comment: Copy to registry.json and edit. Every job is watched through a signal it ALREADY produces - a log it writes, a port it answers on, a container that exists - so nothing you run has to be modified to be covered. max_age_h is how long silence is acceptable; set it to roughly 1.5x the job's own interval.
not_watchable: Anything that runs off this machine and exposes no local signal. Write it down here so the gap is visible rather than forgotten.

jobs.name: Example: a long-running gateway
jobs._why: liveness is process presence - an idle gateway logs nothing, so do not set max_age_h here

jobs.name: Example: a scheduled job that must write a log

error_lines.note: it exits 0 every hour while most of its work fails

jobs._why: exit code 0 with a log full of errors is still a failure

jobs.name: Example: a job that runs on time and does nothing
jobs._why: the failure mode error-alerting can never catch: a clean exit with no output

remedy.reason: look at the log before restarting it

jobs.name: Example: a container
jobs._why: require_restart_policy flags a container running with RestartPolicy=no - it will not come back after a reboot

jobs.name: Example: a service where HTTP 200 is not proof

http.note: sitemap.xml is not returning real XML - a parking page or an error

jobs._why: a status-only check calls a noindex parking page healthy. expect/reject read the body.

remedy.reason: upstream - DNS origin or the host, nothing local can fix it

jobs.name: Example: an app another tool depends on
jobs._why: a desktop app serving a local API. If someone quits it, every agent using that API loses a tool silently.

jobs.name: Example: n8n, proving work happened
jobs._why: a healthy container that has never executed an active workflow is the running-but-doing-nothing case

jobs.name: Example: something you switched off on purpose
jobs._why: reports as OFF, never as ok - so a job you paused for an afternoon does not quietly stay off for a month
